...FINAL INNINGS...

The game's momentum shifted with Babar Azam's dismissal to Kagiso Rabada's exceptional delivery, compounded by Saud Shakeel and Mohammad Rizwan's lapses around the tea break. The trio's failure to capitalize on Pakistan's advantageous position has handed South Africa an opportunity. Pakistan's target of 277 won't be easy to chase, given the spinning pitch and Sajid Khan and Noman Ali's eagerness to exploit it with their bowling. What's in store for us? Let's find out.

South Africa's bowlers sparked a collapse, with Simon Harmer dismissing Mohammad Rizwan in the first over. Salman Agha's resistance wasn't enough to stem the tide, as the tail struggled against quality bowling. Kagiso Rabada's breakthrough with Babar Azam's wicket opened the floodgates, and the Proteas spinners exploited the vulnerability of Pakistan's middle-lower order. South Africa's performance has delighted their team, putting them in a strong position.

From a winning position to an uncomfortable one. A disastrous session pulls South Africa right back into the game. They need 277 runs to win the match. A complete turnaround from them. Even, they will be surprised with how things have unfolded but credit to their spinners, Simon Harmer and Senuran Muthusamy, for doing the job.

South Africa will welcome Saud Shakeel's wicket. Despite their spinners' efforts, they've struggled to claim wickets, except for Kagiso Rabada's crucial breakthrough with Babar Azam's dismissal. The Proteas have faced challenges throughout the innings, and while the current session has produced more turn, they've been inconsistent with line and length. Will Saud Shakeel's wicket be the turning point for South Africa and open the floodgates? Stay tuned to find out as the last session is around the corner.

At the stroke of tea, a brain-fade moment sees Pakistan lose an important wicket of Saud Shakeel, who was batting so well alongside Mohammad Rizwan. It was turning out to be such a good session for Pakistan before the wicket. They have stretched their lead to 259 runs, and with five more wickets in hand and important batters like Mohammad Rizwan and Salman Agha, they'll look to add more runs.

...DAY 3, SESSION 2...

However, the hosts suffered an early setback in their second outing. The spin of Simon Harmer proved relentless, striking twice in quick succession to remove both openers, Imam-ul-Haq and Shan Masood. Leading by 145 runs now, Pakistan desperately need a gritty, crucial stand to consolidate their lead, while South Africa will be sensing a quick haul of wickets. Can South Africa mount a comeback? To find out, tune back in at 7.30 am GMT for all the action after lunch.

An evenly poised session as first Pakistan's spinners stepped up to swiftly mop up the remainder of the South African innings. The tourists were dismissed for 269, handing the home side a handsome first-innings lead of 109 runs. It was a clinical morning spell that saw the last four wickets tumble without much resistance. The damage was done almost entirely by the spin attack. Noman Ali was the chief destroyer, registering a fantastic six-wicket haul. Sajid Khan played the perfect supporting role, claiming three vital scalps to ensure the South African tail did not wag.
A dot to end the session. Much fuller, on off, Abdullah Shafique blocks it back to the bowler. That will be Lunch Break for Day 3!
